rationale.campaign_length: 55 direct Y85 missions define the campaign length.
rationale.colonization: There is some colonization content in the surrounding hills, but it is not the main line.
rationale.complexity: Diplomacy, regional exploration, clans, and financial gates are intertwined.
rationale.dark_story: There are wars with powerful neighbors and clan conflicts, but terroristic policy is not the dominant theme.
rationale.difficulty: The search-for-the-dragon regional requirements and the map situation constrain each other; this has not been tested in play.
rationale.diplomacy: Alliances, accepting kobold minorities, and cooperation with the Blue Scarf movement are important.
rationale.early_pressure: This two-province minor stands between the Command's order and powerful neighbors in Haless.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Balris search, divination, and dragon worship drive the narrative.
rationale.narrative_density: The campaign has a complete turn from the sages' teachings, through the search for the dragon, to constitutional reform.
rationale.tall_play: Clan headquarters, temples, palaces, and banks form a chain of construction prerequisites.
rationale.trade_economy: Gold-mine inflation, banking, and cross-national currency cooperation are important routes.
rationale.warfare: Neighboring states and the Command create expansion pressure.

identity.appearance: A two-province Goldscale Kobold Sage Council theocracy in 1444; Fax Akar is ruler.
identity.formation_scope: Y85 starts as the playable country, with the dragon quest and political reform advancing within the same Tag's missions; a mandatory successor Tag has not been verified.

description.text: Since time immemorial, the people of Yanshen have treasured golden kobold scales as glittering good-luck charms. Many a foreign dignitary has summited the mountains of Balrisen to acquire them, bearing extravagant gifts to exchange in return. It was only a matter of time before the kobolds themselves began to adorn the highest courts in the land. As living portents of good fortune, Goldscale kobolds are honored guests of Yanshen's elite.

description.text:
When Jaher first came to these lands, with hair and spears of gold, we thought him indeed 'Chosen' -- by almighty Balris. Unfortunately, we would learn the truth of the matter in the most awful of ways. After his son Elizar failed in the campaign against Thidinkai, Jaher ordered him confined to camp, and limited to strategic duties. Unfortunately for us, once there, Elizar encountered rumors that 'the hills were filled with gold', and gathered a small expeditionary force to loot said riches and deliver them as restitution to his father.

Of course, these rumors mostly referred to us. We attempted to correct their misunderstanding, but Elizar was not interested in dialogue. His force seized what little riches we had, and smashed the monasteries looking for more. In Elizar's fury and disappointment, he set many ablaze, a monstrous act our people remember as 'The Great Burning'.

Elizar was soon punished, sent back to Bulwar for his sins. But we also remember what happened next: when Jaher was assassinated, the Goldscale kobolds rose up to cast off the elven yoke, and the mountain springs ran red with their blood. Just as it was then, our righteous fervor in defense of Balrijin still burns brighter than any sun.

description.text: Balris the Gold. Bringer of Songs, Slayer of Ignorance, Wisest of Masters. The sagas record that his coming was heralded by a great and thunderous roar, cracking the groundsky and forcing our people to the surface for the first time. By his almighty power, he could have devoured us, enslaved us, or simply driven us away; but he did not. Instead, the Paragon of Benevolence lived alongside our ancestors in the mountain caves, and opened our eyes to a whole new world. Before his countless lessons, our people sung only songs of sorrow and mourning, and built only what we needed to survive. Now, we sing his praises to the golden light of the sunrise, and carve resplendent cliffside temples in his name. And though he only remained with us for a short time, we will never forget his eternal promise: To return one day, and walk alongside us once more. United in his exaltation, under the flag of the Golden Dragon, we named our nation after the object of all our hopes, and our one true god: Balrijin.

description.text: Among the wise Clan Sages of the Golden Council of Balrijin, the Master Sage is chosen to act as the final decider in all disputes. But, in emulation of our patient and benevolent Teacher, Master Sages often decide to remain impartial. There can be only one way resolve such an impasse: a martial arts duel. Known as a 'Dragon Dance', this holy tradition demands we tirelessly hone our skills and train our bodies into brilliant golden weapons, all for the sake of Balrijin's blessed peace. And when we turn those weapons against foreign invaders, they will be all the sharper.

description.text: From the noble courts, Goldscale kobolds proliferated into Yanshen's great cities. Over time, this diaspora evolved into a network of contacts and merchants involved in the lucrative scale trade. In markets and plazas across the land, one can always find a glimmer of gold shining among the crowd, spreading the jewelcrafts and other wares of Balrijin far and wide.

description.text: 'Let's face it, we just can't compete! Try and sell a cloak, they sell a cloak with gold trim! Invent a new gizmo, they'll make the same thing but shinier! How are we supposed to outproduce these lizards when they've got gold falling off their bodies?!' - A very frustrated gnome learning why Goldscales dominate the Yanshen luxury market

description.text: When we first established contact with our western kobold brethren, we were shocked - by their gaudy colors, their crude culture, and the very fact of their existence. It seemed they, too recounted tales of great dragons, but all these wicked 'chromatics' had taught them was to hoard their wealth in giant underground piles. Yet the Wisest of Masters teaches us that true justice lies not in banishing the wicked, but in transfiguring evil to righteousness. We will adopt the western tradition of hoards, but rather than piling up coins and baubles, we will require every kobold who comes of age to submit one of their scales, with a piece of wisdom written on the back. After all, our people are our real treasures - and wisdom is true wealth.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want uninterrupted conquest without prerequisites and do not want to manage cross-regional searches and allied diplomacy.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First, secure the two provinces through alliances and reconcile the clans; in the middle game, follow the dragon clues and build the bank; later, advance constitutional reform and Halessi trade influence.
player_overview.overview: Balrijin is a two-province Goldscale Kobold minor in 1444. The sages preserve the teachings left by the golden dragon Balris, but do not know why he disappeared. You must build alliances between powerful neighbors, reconcile the martial clans, and search for him through libraries, mountains, and divination; afterward, face the challenge that the dragon's return poses to the old clerical power. Banks, cross-cultural cooperation, and council reform make this search for a dragon more than a religious legend. The price is a weak opening and regional missions that require patient preparation.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy a weak-country dragon search, cross-cultural diplomacy, economic institutions, and political reform pulling on one another.
signature_features: The Sage Council, divinatory agents, and regional exploration together form the search-for-the-dragon storyline.
The Goldscale Bank, gold-mine inflation, and cooperation with the Blue Scarf movement turn diplomacy into an economic institution.
Balris' return drives the weakening of the old clerical power and the creation of a council republic.
player_overview.tagline: Help the Goldscale Kobolds find their vanished dragon, then turn a fragile sage state into an open trade republic.

reasons: The search for the golden dragon Balris has a distinctive storyline
Clan diplomacy and the Goldscale Bank connect politics and economics
The late game moves from a theocratic council toward a constitutional republic
warnings: A two-province opening under heavy pressure from powerful neighbors
The search route depends on cross-regional diplomacy and locations

positive_indicators: Accepting human auxiliaries and maintaining cross-cultural alliances
Establishing the Goldscale Bank to stabilize finance
Weakening the old clerical power and advancing a council constitution
values.rationale: Human auxiliaries, cross-cultural diplomacy, financial stability, and constitutional reform express public benefit and recognition across peoples; sage privileges, hostility toward the Command, and policies of dependency for the ruin kingdoms reduce restraint. War and expansion themselves are not counted against the score.
red_flags: Sage and clan privileges in the early search for the dragon
The later protection of ruin kingdoms also envisions dependent relationships
